decision: routed the request to figure-it-out instead of the Feature playbook
why: greenfield product with an engine, storage, a worker and a Spanish site is too many parts for one Feature run

decision: pointed out that three yes/no votes always produce a majority, and asked how consensus works
why: the spec's no-consensus path to the judge could never happen
result: votes are verdadero, falso or no_verificable; 2 of 3 is consensus, else the judge decides

decision: local-first v1: Next.js site plus a separate court worker on this machine, SQLite file
why: the Cursor SDK local runtime needs a long-lived process, and storage sits behind one module so a later Postgres move stays small

decision: logged in through the SDK browser flow instead of an env var
why: the user chose it; the key lives in ~/.cursor/sdk/auth.json for 90 days

decision: picked grok-4.7, gemini-4-argon and claude-opus-5-5 as counsel and grok-4.7 as judge
why: current flagship of each family on this account

decision: tested the riskiest unknown first: can each model research a claim with only web tools and answer through in-process custom tools
why: the whole courtroom design depends on structured tool calls rather than parsing free text
result: VERIFIED: all 3 filed evidence with real URLs and cast a valid vote, 24 to 50 s per turn in parallel

decision: skipped the architect skill and wrote the design directly
why: the spike made the data shape concrete and storage is local and cheap to change; a design bakeoff would cost more than it saves

decision: the court record is an append-only event log, and the claim verdicts are a projection computed from it
why: one source of truth for both the replay page and the verdict badges; no second status field to keep in sync

decision: each turn exposes only the custom tools legal for that phase, through per-send customTools
why: the procedure state machine decides what an agent may do, so an illegal action cannot be called at all

decision: a worker crash mid-trial requeues the case and restarts the trial from an empty record
why: restarting from scratch converges to the same end state; resuming half-finished agent turns would be fragile

decision: tests for the 2-of-3 rule and the projection, then a full scripted session through the same validated tool path the real agents use
why: the judge path cannot be forced with real models, so the scripted court is what proves it

decision: broke the majority rule on purpose (2 to 3) to check the tests catch it
why: the suite passed on the first run, which is a reason to doubt the tests
result: the 2 tests that depend on the rule failed; rule restored

decision: added a dismiss path so the judge can reject a submission with no verifiable claims
why: users will submit opinions; forcing claims out of them would produce fake verdicts

decision: ran a real session on the first case before building the site
why: the full trial with real models was the biggest remaining unknown
result: VERIFIED: 44 events in 10.5 min, A1 verdadero 3 of 3, A2 falso 3 of 3, sources from FIFA, AFA and the city government

decision: marked runtime data paths as ignored for build tracing
why: next build warned the whole project would be bundled into the server output

decision: submitted a case through the real form with a browser script
why: prove the user path, not just the worker
result: VERIFIED: page shows only 'La corte está en sesión' and no claims or votes

decision: removed a duplicate queued case my first form run created when its output was swallowed
why: avoid paying for the same trial twice
result: removed before the worker reached it

decision: redrew the gavel icon
why: the first drawing did not read as a gavel in the screenshot

decision: rendered the judge path from a labeled fixture in a separate data folder on port 3001
why: no real case has split yet, and the seal must look different from Grok's counsel vote
result: VERIFIED visually: seal with gavel and Grok mark, 'Sin mayoría · decidió el juez', struck statement shown

decision: asked a Grok reviewer to audit this log against the run transcript
why: self-review is not a substitute; a different model family reads the trail

decision: let the form-submitted case run to the end and checked its page in the browser
why: prove the full user path: form, worker, verdict page
result: VERIFIED: 78 events in 23 min, 3 claims each with 3 vote icons, 2 real objections both sustained

decision: left partial striking unbuilt and flagged it as an open product call
why: the judge ruled 'ha lugar en parte' on O2 but the model can only strike a whole statement

decision: left session cost and length as they are and reported them
why: 23 min for 3 claims comes mostly from serial objection rounds; cutting them changes the courtroom the user asked for
